extracted.intended_audience: students, coaches, and organizers of math olympiads (USAMO/IMO), and readers interested in contest selection/award rules
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and evaluation criteria used in selecting USA IMO teams and awarding USAMO/IMO honors (medal cutoffs, scholarships, special awards, and honorable-mention rules) as reported in the 2006–2007 USAMO/IMO compilation.

rubrics_metrics.name: IMO medal score thresholds (2005)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gold medals were awarded to students scoring between 35 and 42 points, silver medals to students scoring between 23 and 34 points, and bronze medals to students scoring between 12 and 22 points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context given in the report: there were 513 contestants in the 2005 IMO; counts of medalists (42 gold, 79 silver, 122 bronze) are listed. These numeric score bands are the explicit criterion used in 2005 to assign medal types.

rubrics_metrics.name: IMO medal score thresholds (2006)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gold medals were awarded to students scoring between 28 and 42 points, silver medals to students scoring between 19 and 27 points, and bronze medals to students scoring between 15 and 18 points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context given in the report: there were 498 contestants from 90 countries in the 2006 IMO; counts of medalists (42 gold, 89 silver, 122 bronze) and honorable mentions are listed. These numeric score bands are the explicit criterion used in 2006 to assign medal types (thresholds vary year-to-year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Honorable mention criterion (2006)
rubrics_metrics.description: Honorable mentions were awarded to non-medalists solving at least one problem completely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is stated explicitly in the 2006 contest summary as the rule for awarding honorable mentions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition for perfect papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Contestants who achieved a perfect score on the IMO are noted as having 'perfect papers' (examples: 2005 had 16 perfect papers; 2006 had 3 perfect papers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not a formal award described beyond recognition, 'perfect paper' is used as a performance designation (i.e., attaining full marks across all problems) and is reported as a noteworthy outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: USA team selection rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The USA team members were chosen according to their combined performance on the USAMO and the Team Selection Test that took place at the Mathematical Olympiad Summer Program (MOSP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedural selection rule is stated repeatedly for the years covered (e.g., 'The USA team members were chosen according to their combined performance on the ... USAMO, and the Team Selection Test that took place at the Mathematical Olympiad Summer Program (MOSP)'). MOSP dates and locations are listed in the report for the respective years (e.g., MOSP held at University of Nebraska–Lincoln with given dates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Samuel Greitzer–Murray Klamkin award criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Samuel Greitzer–Murray Klamkin award is given to the top scorer(s) on the USAMO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report names winners in each year and ties; this award is therefore explicitly tied to achieving the top numerical USAMO score(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Akamai Foundation USAMO scholarship awards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Akamai Foundation awards college scholarships to top USAMO finishers; amounts and recipients vary by year as reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from the report: 2005 — top scorers were awarded scholarships of $20,000, $15,000, $5,000, and $5,000 (distributed to the named top finishers); 2006 — $20,000, $15,000, $10,000 for first, second, third; 2007 — $20,000, $15,000, $15,000 (tie for second). The criterion is placement on the USAMO leaderboard as reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clay Mathematics Institute (CMI) award criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: The CMI award is presented for 'a solution of outstanding elegance' and carries a $5,000 cash prize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report identifies the CMI award as an explicit qualitative award tied to judged elegance of a submitted USAMO solution (examples of winners and the problem for which the award was given are cited).
